findings.summary: Trigger D2 refuses Athena's ordinary reuse of CI results by SHA, which is not branch-scoped caching
findings.evidence: Athena already reuses a green CI run for a commit SHA as a normal feature: crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs:10 and :240 ('a reused CI result for the candidate SHA'), verify.rs:162, 405 and 417, run/verification.rs:17, records.rs:828. Any reading about routing or verification that says 'the CI result is reused' or 'a green CI run is reused' will now be refused. The past job fe1df4f's criterion 'a green CI result is reused as the job baseline when the fingerprint matches' (reading.rs:7445) would be refused, and the plan files that as 'unaffected' only because that test asserts a different refuser. These reuses are matched by SHA, not by branch-scoped cache entries, so the five-part save/restore/write/scope statement does not fit them. Words such as CI, run and reused are common in this repository, so the 3% estimate is unlikely to hold. Fix: Narrow D2 to reuse across commits or refs: require a word for another ref or commit in the same segment (early, push, branch, landing, another, previous, base). Or let a statement of the SHA or commit the reused run is matched on satisfy the requirement, by adding sha and commit to the scope words and dropping the write-rights part for D2. Add the fe1df4f sentence, plus one routing-style sentence such as 'a green CI run for the candidate SHA is reused', as accept controls or as deliberate refusals that are justified in the doc comment, and count them in the share estimate.
findings.location: Plan decision 2 / step 2 (trigger D2: CI place + reuse word + result noun); Dependents entry for reading.rs:7445

findings.summary: Building the error from the union of Environment: assumptions hides a missing write-rights part in the common case
findings.evidence: CI_ENVIRONMENT (reading.rs:4469-4470) reads 'Environment: the CI job has write permission to refs on the GitHub origin'. It holds 'write' and 'refs', and readings with a workflow deliverable normally carry such a block. Suppose a reader adds a separate cache line that does not say who writes shared entries. The union then has every part, so the error says 'state all of it in one assumption' and never names the missing write-rights part, which criterion 3 requires. The reader can also pass by pasting the CI block into the cache sentence, which still says nothing about shared cache writes. The plan avoids this only in tests, by choosing a CI block with no write word. So the realistic case goes unshown and the error is wrong in production. Fix: Judge completeness and the missing parts on the Environment: assumptions that name a cache, artifact or result noun. Report the parts missing from the best of them (the one with fewest missing). Use the union only when no assumption names such a noun. Add a test with CI_ENVIRONMENT plus a cache sentence that lacks write rights, and assert that the error names 'which runs may write shared entries'.
findings.location: Plan decision 5 / step 3 (error built from the union of Environment: assumptions); Risks entry 4

findings.summary: The unchanged bail! tail describes the wrong problem when only the cache trigger fires
findings.evidence: surveys.rs:863-867: the tail reads 'nothing in the reading says who performs it, where, with what permissions and what data it reaches'. When only the cache trigger fires, this sentence does not describe the problem (save scope, restore scope and write rights). Fix: When the only trigger is the cache one, use a tail that names cache save scope, restore scope and write rights. Or reword the shared tail so that it covers both cases.
findings.location: Step 3 ('Keep the final bail! tail unchanged')

findings.summary: actions/cache, the usual way to name a GitHub cache, triggers nothing
findings.evidence: scan_segments (surveys.rs:454) splits at any token that contains '/', '_' or '.'. 'actions/cache', the usual way to name a GitHub cache, is therefore dropped. 'The build uses actions/cache keyed by Cargo.lock' fires none of D1, D2 or D3 unless the reading also has a workflow deliverable. Fix: Keep 'actions/cache' and 'actions/upload-artifact' or 'actions/download-artifact' as words, the way 'api.github.com' is kept, and treat them as both a CI place and a cache word. Or list this miss in the limits paragraph.
findings.location: Step 2 (CI place detection) and the doc comment limits

findings.summary: Scope words default, main and pull are common words
findings.evidence: 'default', 'main' and 'pull' are common words ('by default', 'main loop'), so a sentence can meet the scope part without naming a ref. Fix: Accept 'default' only before branch, 'pull' only before request, and 'main' as is. Or list this in the doc comment's lexical limits.

summary: The plan extends the right place: check_environment_reach in surveys.rs, whose word lists, scan_segments, plain_words and environment_assumptions exist as described. It keeps the old doc paragraph and CHANGELOG lookups intact, and its unit-test, corpus and declaration demonstrations use real production seams (check_environment_reach, refusing_check through refuser, replay_declaration, include_str!). I read the dependents I checked (the CI_ENVIRONMENT fixture, the old declaration test at refusal_corpus.rs:2265, the history fixture at reading.rs:7445, and the INPUT_FORMS length), and they match the plan. Two soundness problems need revision. First, the D2 trigger (CI place + reuse word + result noun) matches Athena's own reuse of CI results by SHA in routing and verification, which is not branch-scoped caching. It would refuse the past fe1df4f reading, which the plan waves through because a different assertion is checked. Second, the error is built from the union of Environment: assumptions. Since the usual CI block already holds 'write' and 'refs', the error hides a missing write-rights part, and the tests are fitted to avoid that case instead of fixing it. Both fixes are cheap and leave the design intact.
